correctness.rationale: For fixed 0<a<1, the exact normalized Takenaka–Malmquist basis realizes Q as the transpose of a lower triangular Toeplitz matrix divided by 1-a. Rational matrix identities give A A*+aI=(1+a)^2U with U_ij=min(i,j)+a/(1+a), and its inverse is the specified irreducible positive tridiagonal P, yielding all singular values. The scaled A/N converges in Hilbert–Schmidt norm to (1+a) times Volterra, proving each fixed-rank slope. Row reversal and phase changes make a^N A^(-1) converge in Hilbert–Schmidt norm to rank-one (1+a)a^(r+t), giving the sharp smallest singular a^N. Every quantifier and N=1 boundary is covered; standalone pure-Python rational checker passed 2796 assertions.

value.rationale: The model-space-to-local-Dirichlet inclusion motivates computing exact approximation numbers, a quantitative invariant beyond known embedding conditions and the ordinary spectrum. A complete positive tridiagonal formula and the striking coexistence of linear upper growth and exponential minimum decay reveal sharp nonnormal condition-number behavior and a universal 2/pi derivative-normalized norm limit. These are structural, parameter-uniform in N for each fixed 0<a<1, and directly usable for finite-rank approximation; they are not a routine finite table or a known eigenvalue substitution.
